TechnologyStack.Framework: GitHub repository rendering; React examples use task-specific versions

Migrated pure TypeScript cards preserve the approved TypeScript 5.9 behavior

ContentVocabulary.language-policy: Russian task prose and stable section labels by default; task-specific exceptions require mentor direction.
ContentVocabulary.metadata-labels: Технология; Подборка; Формат; Сложность; Примерное время
ContentVocabulary.technology-policy: Use exactly JavaScript, TypeScript, HTML/CSS, HTML/JavaScript, HTML/CSS/JavaScript, or React/TypeScript.
ContentVocabulary.collection-policy: Use the one approved thematic collection that owns the card; introducing a collection requires mentor approval.
ContentVocabulary.format-policy: Use exactly Написать код, Исправить код, Разобрать код, Предсказать результат, or Приближённая к реальной работе.
ContentVocabulary.difficulty-policy: Use Базовая for one direct concept, Средняя for combined concepts or meaningful approach choice, and Продвинутая for nontrivial execution models, architecture, state, asynchrony, or competing-solution tradeoffs.
ContentVocabulary.duration-policy: Use an integer number of minutes and synchronize it with the thematic and optional interview collection entries.
ContentVocabulary.preservation-policy: Move every source learning goal, prerequisite, and runtime assumption to a visible destination or record a concrete not-applicable reason in CardMigrationEvidence.
ContentVocabulary.environment-policy: Choose one fixed editor profile and declare browser, classic or ESM mode, language, framework, or browser-version assumptions next to the copy/run instruction when they affect behavior.
ContentVocabulary.card-shape-policy: ConciseStudentTaskCard orders title, editor instruction, Условие, one technology-dependent minimal starter or minimum HTML fragment plus JavaScript, three closed hints, closed concise Решение, and closed five-field О задаче; multi-file is real-work only and each included changed solution file is complete with its matching starter FILE path.
ContentVocabulary.javascript-markup-policy: JavaScript cards do not publish full HTML documents, style wrappers, or script wrappers; DOM cards may declare only the minimum semantically necessary HTML fragment before JavaScript.
ContentVocabulary.task-class-policy: Focused tasks have one central action and normally take 10–30 minutes; real-work tasks expose sequential related requirements, normally take 45–60 minutes, and additionally project into collections/real-work/README.md.

profile-Programiz.scope: Console JavaScript without browser API, DOM, or Node-specific semantics
profile-Programiz.copy-run-contract: One complete JavaScript block for main.js.

profile-CodePen.scope: Browser JavaScript, DOM, HTML/CSS, classic script, or ESM
profile-CodePen.copy-run-contract: Use only the minimum required HTML fragment, editable CSS when applicable, and a separate JavaScript block; state classic script or ESM explicitly without publishing script wrappers.

profile-TypeScriptPlayground.copy-run-contract: One complete TypeScript block; multiple files are permitted only for a real-work task whose target editor can reproduce the declared file boundaries.

profile-ReactTypeScript.scope: React and TypeScript with React 19.2 behavior
profile-ReactTypeScript.copy-run-contract: Replace src/App.tsx completely; add files only for a real-work task with genuine file boundaries, and include only complete changed files with matching FILE paths in its solution.

PreferredAgentStack.preferred-content-format: GitHub Flavored Markdown with relative repository links
PreferredAgentStack.preferred-progressive-disclosure: Exactly three independent closed hint details blocks, then closed concise solution and closed five-field metadata
PreferredAgentStack.preferred-verification: Strict structural, preservation, content, synchronization, target-editor, browser, link, XML, and GitHub rendered-view evidence; temporary harnesses are diagnostic only
PreferredAgentStack.preferred-grace-resolution: Resolve grace from PATH, then fall back to $HOME/.bun/bin/grace before treating the CLI as unavailable.

discouraged-surface.reason: The initial project intentionally has no repository runtime.

PreferredAgentStack.discouraged-surface: catalog generators, site frameworks, and package-manager-based Markdown pipelines

module-level.command: Verify ConciseStudentTaskCard order, task class, preservation ledger, minimal copy-ready code, FILE parity where justified, three exact hints, five metadata fields, thematic and optional real-work membership, and final target-editor expected, actual, and verdict.
module-level.focus: Prove concise document structure, source-contract preservation, and solution behavior in the named online editor without adding a permanent repository runtime.

wave-level.command: Validate the serialized 8 + 8 + 5 concise redesign units; compare each changed card with exactly one thematic, zero or one interview, and supported real-work entry, graph and verification facts, resolve links, record CardMigrationEvidence, push the focused commit, and capture required rendered evidence.
wave-level.focus: Prove migration quality and atomic synchronization across card, collections, knowledge graph, verification plan, and Beads evidence.

phase-level.command: Run xmllint on docs/*.xml, scan changed files for whitespace and placeholder defects, review the full catalog projection, and inspect GitHub rendering when template or HTML markup changes.
phase-level.focus: Repository-wide structural integrity and student-visible GitHub behavior.

Testing.mocking-policy: Use embedded fixtures, deterministic adapters, or fake clocks when network, time, or external state would otherwise make the task non-repeatable; do not mock away the behavior being taught or substitute a harness for final target-editor evidence.

Observability.evidence-format: module-id, verification-ref, artifact-path, mode, editor-profile, preservation-ledger, expected, actual, verdict, collection-sync
Observability.required-fields: moduleId, verificationRef, candidateId, artifactPath, validationDecision, slug, mode, editorProfile, sourceLearningGoal, sourcePrerequisite, sourceRuntimeAssumption, destinationLocations, targetEditorExpectedResult, targetEditorActualResult, verdict, thematicCollection, interviewCollection, realWorkCollection, graphVerificationSync, beadsIssueId
Observability.stable-anchors: Условие; Подсказка 1 — куда смотреть; Подсказка 2 — с чего начать; Подсказка 3 — почти решение; Решение; О задаче
Observability.redaction: Never place secrets, credentials, private student data, or proprietary source material in task cards or evidence.

AutonomyPolicy.replan-trigger: Ambiguous metadata, collection, editor, task class, or profile; duplicate learning goal; missing prerequisite or asset; unnecessary multi-file split; full-document JavaScript wrapper; card/collection or real-work contradiction; unexpected GitHub rendering; unavailable mandatory evidence; or a solution requiring undeclared knowledge.
AutonomyPolicy.checkpoint-requirement: Every task change reports mode, editor profile, preservation ledger, artifacts changed, checks run, target-editor expected/actual/verdict, collection sync, remaining risk, and next action.

DeliveryShape.shape: GitHub repository whose root README is a short student hub, whose fourteen target collections are the primary selection surface, and whose twenty-one target task directories render concise copy-ready self-contained Markdown cards.
DeliveryShape.implementation-state: The prior twenty-card, thirteen-collection catalog remains implemented. ConciseStudentTaskCard, the twenty-slug temporary compatibility state, three serialized 8 + 8 + 5 waves, the twenty-one-card and fourteen-collection cutover, and the rendered audit are staged as planned Phases 16 through 20; no future card or collection is claimed implemented.
